reviews.reader_notes: Several sources the note tagged [abstract] or [search only] are open in PMC and were read whole here: Vijayan 2019 (PMC8650759), Bao 2026 (PMC12893610), Kim 2025 (PMC12283916), Achar 2023 (PMC10538057), Gotschi 2026 (PMC13181670, CC BY-NC-ND 4.0), Tsagkaris 2023 (PMC10639121) and the Neurosurgical Review 2026 systematic review (PMID 41840102 is PMC12992485, Neurosurg Rev 49(1):283), so their tags can be upgraded when the fixes land; Europe PMC also lists a Blomenkamp 2024 EMBC paper (PMID 40039560, 'Reconstruction of 3D lumbar spine models from incomplete segmentations using landmark detection') that may be the geometric method Da Mutten names. The README row's counts (20 methods tabled, 2 public test sets, 3 public code items) and its closest-to-naming-levels text match the note, but the Vijayan finding makes a third partly public atlas (30 of 40 members from TCIA and SpineWeb, leave-one-out) and the grotyx finding adds a fourth public code item (MIT) that computes a geometric isthmus width, so the README's 2 and 3 may need the same qualification. Every other row and bullet checked held: the 42-paper note's Lien, Zindrick, Busscher (item 4), Shin 2024, Duman 2026 (T11 to L2, 517 adults) and 'checked only in the lumbar spine and refuses the pedicle' lines are there verbatim or in substance, the four 'without masks' notes name the pedicle only in ct_intensity_methods.md (step 6 of its section 6 Inferences and the Gaps of its section 7), the benchmark notes carry no pedicle term, and the Tomography 2026 (PMID 41893835, 12(3):40) and Eur J Radiol 2021 (PMID 34700094, 144:109999) records exist as described.
reviews.refuter_notes:
Every source was read in full by curl through the proxy: Europe PMC fullTextXML, NCBI efetch for PMC8650759 and PMC9148916, arXiv API, arXiv and ar5iv HTML, raw GitHub, the OpenReview API, the Folia journal PDF and the IAS abstract page. I made 1 WebFetch call (the VID GitHub page) and no WebSearch. Scratch files are in <session scratchpad>/refute-pedicles/dl.

Two findings were refuted:
- gotschi2026-runtime: the reader confused the runtime with the lower IQR bound of the 58.6 percent misalignment figure. The paper prints 5.4 min median runtime itself.
- sonogym-neurips: OpenReview lists SonoGym at NeurIPS 2025 Datasets and Benchmarks Track (forum SRStCEJ0Qu). The note could name the track and tag it [page, OpenReview].

Corrections to the reader's fixes:
- SafeRPlan: the reader said it uses no ultrasound. Its arXiv full text does reconstruct the dorsal surface from a simulated ultrasound scan. The models are MRI-derived (L1 to L5), not CT-derived, and no code was found.
- Bao: the figure caption's 405 patients disagrees with Table 1's 320 + 37 = 357.
- Achar: the reader's '11 defects on three spines' is not verified; only n = 11 defects is.

Scherer 2022: the full text in Spine J is not on PMC. The 2023 J Clin Med paper (PMC10094754) gives no levels for the 2022 training set, so the levels remain unknown.

Side observations outside the findings:
- Vijayan 2019 names 2 lumbosacral transitional vertebrae among its 9 registration outliers.
- Goerres' abstract gives the L3 pedicle-centre deviation as 1.12 +/- 0.67 mm and the diameter difference as 1.26 +/- 1.19 mm, not the note's 1.16, 1.09 and 1.09 to 1.58.
- The C2-NET repository has train.py and C3D_model.py on main, and LICENSE returns 404.
